test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper( Held On: 16 Jan 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A glass cylinder with diameter 20 cm has water to a height of 9 cm. A metal cube of 8 cm edge is immersed in it completely. Calculate the height (correct to I decimal place) by which the water will rise in the cylinder (by taking π = 3.142).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Rise in height** (h) = **Volume of immersed object** ÷ **Base area of cylinder**

h = 8³ ÷ (π × 10²)

h = 512 ÷ (3.142 × 100) = 512 ÷ 314.2

h ≈ 1.629 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 1.6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Diameter of **cylinder** = 20 cm ⇒ Radius (r) = 10 cm

Edge of **metal cube** (a) = 8 cm

Value of π = 3.142

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8917d644c78146ef8150a56d6835fff78b1cc8f4f828367804d8415f602f3853.png] 

**Formula:**

Volume of **water displaced** = Volume of **metal cube**

π × r² × h = a³

**Calculations:**

⇒ 3.142 × 10 × 10 × h = 8 × 8 × 8

⇒ 314.2 × h = 512

⇒ h = 512 ÷ 314.2

⇒ h = 1.6295...

⇒ h ≈ 1.6 cm (correct to 1 decimal place)

**∴ The correct answer is 1.6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Archimedes Principle (Volume)

When an object is completely immersed in a liquid, the **volume of liquid displaced** is equal to the **volume of the object**.

Cylinder and Cube Volumes

Volume of Cylinder = πr²h and Volume of Cube = a³, where r is radius, h is height, and a is the edge.

Rise in Liquid Level

Rise in height (h) = Volume of solid ÷ Area of the cross-section of the container.</p
